subject: Clarify: pen-test trigger / inspection scope and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@clearmaphealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearmaphealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pen-test trigger language — need clarification

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the draft Order Form. A couple of items jumped out from our counsel's review related to the security exhibit: specifically the pen-test/inspection trigger and what "inspection access" actually permits. Our legal team wants to avoid broad "inspection" language that could be interpreted as unlimited production access or extensive data exports. Two asks from our side:

1) Can you share the intended scope when Redwood mentions "inspection access" in the exhibit? e.g., limited to non-prod/staging, timeboxed, or read-only logs?

2) What triggers a pen-test or on-site inspection under your language — is it customer request, regulatory requirement, or a security incident? We need clear, objective triggers so we can commit to windows.

Jamie (and counsel) also asked whether Redwood would accept (a) pen-test scope pre-approval, (b) a maximum number of test-days per year, and (c) an evidence cadence (we asked for weekly snapshots and SOC 2 report availability). I've attached our assessment summary for context.

Can you propose specific redline language we can take to counsel? We're trying to avoid an open-ended audit right if we can find a mutually bounded alternative.

Thanks,

Jamie Lee
Head of Legal Ops
ClearMap Health
[Attachment: ClearMap_Assessment-Summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@clearmaphealth.com>
Cc: legal@clearmaphealth.com, kirthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pen-test trigger language — need clarification

Jamie — thanks for the clear ask and the summary. We hear the concern about open-ended "inspection" language. High level proposal from our side:

- Define "inspection" in the Security Exhibit as: mutually agreed scope, non-production environment access by default, read-only access to logs and telemetry, and no bulk exports of customer data unless expressly authorized in writing.
- Pen-test trigger: may be initiated by (i) a customer request with 30 days' notice, (ii) a regulatory or legal obligation, or (iii) a high-severity incident where forensic testing is required. For customer-initiated tests we'll require advance scope approval and a test window (max 5 business days unless both parties agree).
- Evidence cadence: weekly operational snapshots (log slices + configuration manifest) during the test window; SOC 2 reports available upon NDA/portal access; we can commit to a recorded runbook for evidence handoff.

I'll loop in Legal and Product Operations to finalize redline text. Attached is a working draft of the Security Exhibit (v2) that includes this wording — please review and tell us what you'd like tightened. If this looks reasonable to counsel, we can push the redlines into the Order Form and send a DocuSign bundle.

Action items: internal review (Karthik/Laura) for legal + operational feasibility, then I will reply with firm redline text.

Regards,

Priyom Das
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v2.docx (docx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Pen-test trigger language — internal redlines

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 10:03 AM Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll loop in Legal and Product Operations to finalize redline text.

Thanks — quick legal take and suggested redline snippets:

1) Replace "inspection access" with a defined term in Exhibit A: "Inspection Access means limited, timeboxed, and mutually agreed access to Customer-specific operational artifacts, logs, and configuration in a non-production environment; does not include the right to extract or copy Protected Health Information or other regulated data unless explicitly approved in writing."

2) For pen-tests: add clause that customer-initiated tests require (a) 30 days' written notice, (b) a scope document signed by both parties, and (c) proof that test tools will not attempt data exfiltration. Cap tests at 5 business days per rolling 12-month period unless both parties agree to an extension.

3) Evidence and SOC2: add a binding commitment that Redwood will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report within 10 business days of request (subject to NDA) and will schedule operational evidence handoff calls with a 3-business-day turnaround during a test window.

I'll prepare exact redline markup and include fallback language (if we cannot provide non-prod access, Redwood will provide a sanitized logs package for forensic review).

-Karthik
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@clearmaphealth.com>
Cc: legal@clearmaphealth.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: agreed exhibit wording and next steps

Jamie — thanks for the patience while we worked through counsel and ops. Below is the agreed, customer-facing summary and next steps; the redline has been applied to the Security Exhibit v2 and attached.

Summary of agreed points (to be reflected in Exhibit A):
- "Inspection Access" definition: mutually agreed in writing; default environment is non-production/staging; access limited to read-only logs, telemetry, and configuration manifests; no bulk export of PHI or regulated data without specific written authorization.
- Pen-test trigger & limits: customer may request a pen-test with 30 days' written notice; scope must be approved by both parties; tests are capped at 5 business days per rolling 12 months unless extended by mutual agreement; Redwood retains the right to suspend or require additional controls for tests that pose a production stability risk.
- Evidence cadence: during test windows Redwood will provide weekly operational snapshots and a scheduled evidence handoff call with a 3-business-day turnaround for follow-up artifacts; SOC 2 Type II reports are available to customer under NDA via our secure portal (we will provide the latest report within 10 business days of request).

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Exhibit_v2.docx (redlines included); OrderForm-Redlines.pdf (summarized).

Next steps:
1) If counsel at ClearMap is aligned, confirm and we will upload revised Order Form to DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123-redwood-clearMap
2) If you want a limited test window calendar, Jordan (cc'd) can propose available windows to align with procurement timing.
3) If any of the defined limits are unacceptable, please flag which clause and we will discuss carveouts.

We believe this preserves ClearMap's need for auditability while keeping scope operationally safe for Redwood's shared infrastructure. Let me know if you'd like a short call to walk the redlines live.

Best,

Priyom Das
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
